name: CheckinBee
tagline: A daily check-in app for seniors living alone
daily_ok_verdict: CheckinBee is the closest category match here: like Daily OK, it's a software daily check-in app — the senior confirms they're OK and contacts are notified if they don't. Because the concept overlaps, the honest comparison is about emphasis, not category. Daily OK is built first for the adult-child caregiver and the family around them — sibling-shareable Viewers, tiered plans, mood and consistency pattern signals, and Critical Alerts that can bypass Do Not Disturb on Family+. If you want the simplest possible single-sender check-in, either app does the core job. If you want the daily check-in to sit inside a small family coordination system with escalation and trend visibility, that's where Daily OK is aimed. Feature specifics on either side change often — verify current details on both sites.

migration_guide: List the three things that matter most to your family (e.g. sibling sharing, escalation behavior, pattern signals, Do Not Disturb bypass).
Open both apps' current feature and pricing pages side by side — details on either side change over time.
Trial Daily OK free for 7 days with your actual check-in time and your real escalation contacts.
Check that escalation timing and who-gets-alerted-first match how your family actually wants to be notified.
If switching, export or note any history you want to keep from the other app first.
Pick the one whose default behavior needs the least configuration to match your family's expectations.

faqs.q: Aren't Daily OK and CheckinBee basically the same?
faqs.a: They're in the same category — software daily check-in apps with escalation. The difference is emphasis: Daily OK is built around the adult-child caregiver and the family (shared Viewers, tiered plans, pattern signals, Critical Alerts). Compare current features on both sites for your specific need.
Both are low-cost, no-hardware apps and pricing changes over time. Daily OK starts at $3.99/month; confirm CheckinBee's current pricing on their site rather than relying on any third-party figure.
No. Neither is a medical device. Both record a daily check-in and notify contacts if it's missed — they don't detect falls or vitals.

faqs.q: Can I try Daily OK before switching?
faqs.a: Yes — every Daily OK plan has a 7-day free trial, so you can test it with your real check-in time and contacts before committing.

faqs.q: Why does this page say 'verify on their site' so often?
faqs.a: Because feature sets and prices for both apps change, and publishing stale specifics about a competitor would be misleading. We state Daily OK's specifics and point you to CheckinBee's own site for theirs.
